titre: Adding my child to my health insurance, getting their certificate of entitlement and carte Vitale
resume: Add the child to both parents' carte Vitale, download their certificate of entitlement on ameli, and request their own carte Vitale from 12 to 15 or from age 16.
aQuoiCaSert: A child under 16 is covered as a dependent (ayant droit) of one or both parents. When the child is listed on both parents' carte Vitale (health insurance card), the parent who takes them to the doctor or pharmacy is reimbursed directly: this is very useful when parents are separated. The certificate of entitlement (attestation de droits) proves that the child is covered; daycare, school, leisure centers and hospitals often ask for it. Finally, a child can have their own carte Vitale, at a parent's request from 12 to 15, and from age 16. In Réunion, the Assurance Maladie (French public health insurance) is managed by the CGSS (Caisse générale de sécurité sociale, the general social security fund).
quiEstConcerne: Parents of a newborn, or of a child covered under only one of the two parents.
Separated parents who each want to be reimbursed for the child's healthcare.
Parents who are asked for a certificate of entitlement (daycare, school, holiday camp, hospital).
Young people aged 12 to 18 who need their own carte Vitale.
aSavoir: A child can be added to both parents whatever the family situation, if each parent is insured. The reimbursement goes to the parent whose carte Vitale was presented. If one parent is no longer insured, reimbursements go to the other.

Online, the procedure is done from the ameli account (the French health insurance website), using the file of the parent whose card the child is already on. By post: Cerfa n° 14445 with a copy of the up-to-date family record book (livret de famille) or an extract of the birth certificate.
Certificate of entitlement: it can be downloaded free of charge in the ameli account (website or app). If the child does not appear, they are not yet linked to your file.

Child's carte Vitale: from 12 to 15, at a parent's request; from 16, with the consent of a parent who holds parental authority. It is free. At 16, the Assurance Maladie sends a letter and the card arrives in about 3 weeks.
Attach bank details (RIB) in the young person's name if you want their reimbursements paid directly to them. A parent can block their minor child's access to the carte Vitale app.
From 16 to 18, the young person can remain their parents' dependent or become an independent beneficiary. The link ends if they work, including as an apprentice.

documents.libelle: Copy of the up-to-date family record book or an extract of the child's birth certificate
documents.detail: Only one of these is needed to add the child. Birth certificate free online on service-public.gouv.fr or from the town hall (mairie) of the place of birth.

documents.libelle: Form Cerfa n° 14445, if you add the child by post
documents.detail: Completed and signed, sent to the CGSS de La Réunion.

documents.libelle: Guardianship judgment or proof of care, if you are not the parent
documents.detail: Copy. For a guardian or a person who has taken in the child.

documents.libelle: Recent ID photo of the child, for their carte Vitale
documents.detail: Online, a scanned photo is enough.

documents.libelle: Child's ID, for their carte Vitale
documents.detail: Copy or scan of their ID card or passport.

documents.libelle: Bank details (RIB) in the young person's name
documents.detail: Optional, so they are reimbursed into their own account.

documents.libelle: Certificate of entitlement listing the child
documents.detail: Free to download on ameli. Get a new one if your situation changes.

etapes.titre: Check which carte Vitale the child is on
etapes.detail: In your ameli account, beneficiaries section, or at a pharmacy.

etapes.titre: Add the child to the other parent's card
etapes.detail: From the ameli account, or by post with Cerfa n° 14445 and a copy of the family record book or the birth certificate.
In the ameli account, procedures section: select the child. Without an account, call 36 46.

etapes.titre: Request the child's carte Vitale if needed
etapes.detail: From the ameli account of the parent the child is linked to, with their scanned photo and ID, or with a form sent to the insurance fund.
If you go to a CGSS office: your carte Vitale, your ID, the family record book or the child's birth certificate, their photo and ID for a carte Vitale, and the guardianship judgment if applicable.
At a pharmacy or a self-service terminal, once the change has been recorded.

ou.detail: Adding a child, certificate of entitlement, ordering a carte Vitale.
